steps.title: Prepare BAL suture
steps.instruction: Cut a 4 cm length of suture, tie an overhand knot leaving at least 1.5 cm of suture on each side of the knot.

steps.title: Prepare BAL needle with tubing
steps.instruction: Cut 2.5 cm of polyethylene tubing (0.58 mm × 0.965 mm × 30.5 mm). Slide the tubing onto a 23‑gauge, 1‑inch needle of a 1 mL syringe so that the needle bevel is fully covered and ~0.2 cm of tubing extends past the tip.

steps.title: Anesthetize mouse for vaccination
steps.instruction: Induce anesthesia with an approved inhaled or injectable agent, then place the mouse in your hand and monitor respiration (≈1 breath every 2–3 s).

steps.title: Load vaccine into pipette
steps.instruction: Load the vaccine (or other liquid) into a pipette; prepare either a single 25 µL bolus or two 20 µL boluses depending on desired volume.

steps.title: Position mouse for intranasal delivery
steps.instruction: Place the mouse supine in the palm of the non‑dominant hand, trace a light line with the thumb from the xyphoid process over the throat to the jaw, keep the jaw closed, and tilt the mouse to a ~60° incline.

steps.title: Instill intranasal dose
steps.instruction: Hold the loaded pipette above the nares, depress the plunger slowly to place a droplet, wait for the mouse to inhale, then wait an additional breath before delivering the next droplet if a second bolus is required.

substeps.instruction: If bubbling occurs, aspirate the liquid with the pipette and re‑administer.
Maintain the 60° position for 2–3 breaths after each droplet.
Feel for turbulence on the chest to confirm inhalation.

steps.title: Recover mouse post‑vaccination
steps.instruction: Remove the thumb from the jaw, place it on the chest, depress lightly, then return the mouse to its cage in a supine position to recover.

steps.title: Anesthetize mouse for BAL
steps.instruction: Anesthetize the mouse (gaseous or injectable) and keep it supine; avoid anesthetizing multiple mice simultaneously and do not sacrifice by cervical dislocation.

steps.title: Dissect thoracic block and expose trachea
steps.instruction: Soak abdomen and thorax with 70 % ethanol, make an abdominal incision toward the rib cage, laterally displace abdominal organs, sharply dissect the abdominal artery, perforate and remove the diaphragm, push lungs medially, dissect laterally through the rib cage, grip the rib cage, pull superiorly to expose the trachea, clean any residual blood with sterile gauze.

substeps.instruction: If the trachea remains hidden after step 25, sharply dissect throat tissue to expose it.

steps.title: Cannulate trachea with BAL needle
steps.instruction: Pass the prepared suture loop over the most superior part of the trachea, load the BAL needle with 250 µL ice‑cold PBS, insert the needle halfway down the trachea (avoiding the esophagus) ensuring the beveled tip is fully concealed by the tubing, then tighten the suture tightly around the trachea and needle shaft.

substeps.instruction: Verify needle depth and suture position with forceps.

steps.title: Perform conventional BAL (first two washes)
steps.instruction: Lift the lung block onto the syringe, support the lungs, hold the syringe vertically, gently depress the plunger to inflate both lobes, then slowly pull back to aspirate the PBS; repeat for a second 250 µL instillation, collecting each recovered volume into a 1.5 mL tube kept on ice.

substeps.instruction: If resistance is felt, adjust needle angle and repeat steps 35‑37 until ~100–200 µL is recovered per 250 µL instillation.

steps.title: Perform exhaustive BAL (three 300 µL washes)
steps.instruction: Using the same syringe, aspirate 300 µL ice‑cold PBS, re‑attach to the needle, repeat the inflate‑aspirate cycle, and collect each recovered volume into a fresh 1.5 mL tube; repeat this wash two more times (total 900 µL) and keep the final tube on ice.

steps.title: Collect lung lobes and optional perfusion
steps.instruction: Dissect lung lobes from the thoracic block with scissors and forceps, place them into pre‑labeled 1.5 mL tubes containing 750 µL cell culture media on ice. Optionally, perfuse by injecting 5 mL ice‑cold perfusion buffer into the right ventricle with a 23G needle until the lungs blanch.

substeps.instruction: Note: perfusion does not remove vascular‑bound leukocytes; intravenous labeling is required for that.

steps.title: Centrifuge BAL fractions
steps.instruction: Spin all 1.5 mL tubes (conventional and exhaustive fractions) at 3,000 × g, 4 °C for 5 min in a tabletop microcentrifuge.

steps.title: Separate supernatant and cell pellets
steps.instruction: Visualize pellets; transfer the supernatant from the conventional fraction to a fresh tube and store at –20 °C; discard the exhaustive supernatant as liquid waste; resuspend the conventional pellet in 200 µL cell culture media, then combine with the exhaustive pellet and keep on ice.

steps.title: Count BAL cells and assess viability
steps.instruction: Enumerate cells using a hemocytometer or automated counter and assess viability with trypan blue; expect 3–5 × 10⁵ cells from a naïve mouse.

steps.title: Mince lung tissue for mononuclear isolation
steps.instruction: Using surgical scissors, mince each lung lobe into small pieces directly in its 1.5 mL collection tube; avoid bead‑based homogenizers to preserve viability.

steps.title: Digest lung tissue
steps.instruction: Transfer minced tissue to a sterile 50 mL polypropylene tube, add 10 mL lung digestion solution (exact composition not specified), rinse the original 1.5 mL tube with additional digestion solution, then incubate at 37 °C, 225 rpm shaking for 1 h (or manually swirl every 10–15 min if no shaker).

steps.title: Filter digested tissue
steps.instruction: Pass the digested suspension through a 100 µm nylon mesh basket into a fresh 50 mL tube, grinding the tissue through the mesh with the rubber end of a 5 mL syringe plunger, rinsing the mesh intermittently with ice‑cold RPMI‑1640; repeat until all visible pieces are filtered.

steps.title: Centrifuge and lyse red blood cells
steps.instruction: Spin the filtered suspension at 500 × g, 4 °C for 5 min, discard supernatant, resuspend the pellet in 1 mL RBC lysis solution, add an additional 1 mL lysis solution (total 2 mL), incubate 2 min at 18–25 °C with gentle swirling, then stop lysis by adding 40 mL ice‑cold PBS.

steps.title: Wash and resuspend lung mononuclear cells
steps.instruction: Filter the lysed suspension through a fresh 100 µm mesh, centrifuge at 500 × g, 4 °C for 5 min, discard supernatant, briefly invert tube on low‑particulate wipes to remove residual liquid, resuspend the pellet in 1 mL complete cell culture media, keep on ice.

steps.title: Count lung mononuclear cells
steps.instruction: Enumerate cells and assess viability with trypan blue; cells should retain >95 % viability.

steps.title: Plate cells for Trm staining (optional stimulation)
steps.instruction: Add 5 × 10⁵–2 × 10⁶ lung mononuclear cells or 3–5 × 10⁵ BAL cells to each well of a 96‑well U‑bottom plate in 200 µL total volume. For antigen‑specific stimulation, add peptide pools at 2 µg/mL final concentration (final volume 200 µL) and 50 µL Brefeldin A working solution per well, then incubate 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 6 h before staining.

steps.title: Viability LIVE/DEAD staining (Trm)
steps.instruction: Centrifuge plate at 500 × g, 4 °C for 5 min, discard supernatant, resuspend pellets in 200 µL ice‑cold PBS, centrifuge again (500 × g, 4 °C, 5 min), discard supernatant, add 50 µL Aqua LIVE/DEAD working solution (1:100 dilution in PBS) to each well (except unstained control), incubate 18–25 °C for 20 min protected from light, then add 150 µL ice‑cold PBS, centrifuge (500 × g, 4 °C, 5 min) and discard supernatant.

steps.title: Fc block staining (Trm)
steps.instruction: Resuspend cells in 50 µL Fc Block working solution (0.5 mg/mL stock diluted 1:100 in ice‑cold buffer), incubate on ice 15 min protected from light, add 150 µL ice‑cold FACS buffer, centrifuge 500 × g, 4 °C, 5 min, discard supernatant.

steps.title: Extracellular stain Trm Mix #1
steps.instruction: Prepare Trm Master Mix #1 by adding CD103‑Biotin (0.5 mg/mL stock, 1:100 dilution) to ice‑cold buffer; resuspend cells in 50 µL of this mix, incubate on ice 30 min protected from light, add 150 µL ice‑cold FACS buffer, centrifuge 500 × g, 4 °C, 5 min, discard supernatant.

steps.title: Extracellular stain Trm Mix #2
steps.instruction: Prepare Trm Master Mix #2 containing: CD4‑APC‑Cy7 (0.2 mg/mL, 1:400), CD8‑PE‑Cy7 (0.2 mg/mL, 1:400), CD44‑PE (0.2 mg/mL, 1:800), Streptavidin‑QDot800 (1 µM, 1:500), CD11a‑FITC (0.5 mg/mL, 1:100), CD49a‑AF647 (0.2 mg/mL, 1:100), CD69‑BV605 (0.2 mg/mL, 1:100); resuspend cells in 50 µL of this mix, incubate on ice 30 min protected from light, add 150 µL ice‑cold FACS buffer, centrifuge 500 × g, 4 °C, 5 min, discard supernatant.

steps.title: Intracellular fixation/permeabilization (Trm)
steps.instruction: Resuspend cells in 100 µL Cytofix/Cytoperm, incubate 4 °C for 20 min protected from light, centrifuge 500 × g, 4 °C, 5 min, discard supernatant, resuspend in 200 µL 1× Permwash, centrifuge 750 × g, 4 °C, 5 min; (pause point – cells can be stored in 200 µL PBS at 4 °C up to 24 h).

steps.title: Intracellular stain Trm Mix #3
steps.instruction: Prepare Trm Master Mix #3 with CD3‑V450 (0.2 mg/mL, 1:200); resuspend cells in 50 µL of this mix, incubate on ice 30 min protected from light, add 150 µL 1× Permwash, centrifuge 750 × g, 4 °C, 5 min, discard supernatant, resuspend in 200 µL FACS buffer. Samples are now ready for flow cytometry.

steps.title: Plate cells for macrophage staining
steps.instruction: Add 5 × 10⁵–2 × 10⁶ lung mononuclear cells or 3–5 × 10⁵ BAL cells to each well of a 96‑well U‑bottom plate in 200 µL total volume (prepare FMO/isotype controls as needed).

steps.title: Viability LIVE/DEAD staining (macrophage)
steps.instruction: Centrifuge plate 500 × g, 4 °C, 5 min, discard supernatant, resuspend pellets in 200 µL ice‑cold PBS, centrifuge again (500 × g, 4 °C, 5 min), add 50 µL Aqua LIVE/DEAD working solution (1:100 in PBS) to each well except unstained control, incubate 18–25 °C for 20 min protected from light, add 150 µL ice‑cold PBS, centrifuge 500 × g, 4 °C, 5 min, discard supernatant.

steps.title: Fc block staining (macrophage)
steps.instruction: Resuspend cells in 50 µL Fc Block working solution (0.5 mg/mL stock, 1:100 dilution), incubate on ice 15 min protected from light, add 150 µL ice‑cold FACS buffer, centrifuge 500 × g, 4 °C, 5 min, discard supernatant.

steps.title: Extracellular stain APC Mix #1
steps.instruction: Prepare APC Master Mix #1 containing: CD64‑PE (0.2 mg/mL, 1:100), Ly6C‑Biotin (0.5 mg/mL, 1:200), CD11c‑APC (0.2 mg/mL, 1:200), B220‑V450 (0.2 mg/mL, 1:200), CD3‑PerCp‑Cy5.5 (0.2 mg/mL, 1:200), CD45‑APC‑Cy7 (0.2 mg/mL, 1:400), CD11b‑PE‑Cy7 (0.2 mg/mL, 1:400), Ly6G‑BV605 (0.2 mg/mL, 1:500), CD24‑BV650 (0.2 mg/mL, 1:1500), SiglecF‑PE‑CF594 (0.2 mg/mL, 1:1500); resuspend cells in 50 µL of this mix, incubate on ice 30 min protected from light, add 150 µL ice‑cold FACS buffer, centrifuge 500 × g, 4 °C, 5 min, discard supernatant.

steps.title: Extracellular stain APC Mix #2
steps.instruction: Prepare APC Master Mix #2 with Streptavidin‑QDot800 (1 µM, 1:500 dilution, ice); resuspend cells in 50 µL of this mix, incubate on ice 30 min protected from light, add 150 µL ice‑cold FACS buffer, centrifuge 500 × g, 4 °C, 5 min, discard supernatant, resuspend in 200 µL FACS buffer. Samples are ready for flow cytometry.

description: The experimental techniques and downstream flow cytometric analysis detailed in this protocol are based on samples from mice intranasally vaccinated with a next-generation trivalent chimpanzee adenovirus-vectored COVID-19 vaccine candidate (Afkhami et al., 2022). This protocol has wide applicability and has been utilized to assess immunogenicity from mucosal vaccines for Mycobacterium tuberculosis and influenza A virus, primary immune responses to bacterial/viral infection, and to noxious stimuli such as cigarette smoke (Afkhami et al., 2019; D’Agostino et al., 2020; McGrath et al., 2022; Yao et al., 2018). Moreover, widespread use of these standardized techniques will be critical for pre-clinical evaluation of next-generation vaccines or therapeutic treatments for any mucosal pathogen.
